## Orientation

Write root: `/home/andrewyin/orchestra/.worktrees/library-e2e--fix-library-e2e-coverage` on `task/library-e2e/fix-library-e2e-coverage`.

The phase review rejected `tests/test_library_e2e.py` as a spec-gap. This fix edits that file. Do not add a second test file as a substitute.

### Work-item (quote)

## Description

Fix the spec-gap that blocked the phase review. One integration test must build the temporary repository, read the created record with open_store, run orchestra close-batch to exit 0, call the Python close on that same fixture, fail if that call starts aff or adaptive-artifacts, and fail unless that Python close accepts the fixture.

## Approach

Extend tests/test_library_e2e.py, the one integration test. Assert open_store sees the record adaptive-artifacts create wrote. Call close_batch.main on that fixture and assert it returns 0. Record subprocesses for that call and fail if any is aff or adaptive-artifacts. Do not discard bind failures. Do not add a second test file as a substitute.

### Requirements (quote by id)

R4: `adaptive-artifacts create` run in that repository writes a record into the store `open_store` opens for it.
R5: `orchestra close-batch` run as a command in that repository exits 0 for a close that meets the claim gate.
R6: The Python close function on that repository does not start a process for `aff` or `adaptive-artifacts`.

### Design / decisions (quote)

## Invariants

Command close and Python close both accept the same fixture. The in-process close does not spawn the other commands.

## Assumptions

The three packages are installed in the test environment. Claim-gate behavior follows whatever `claim-clocks` has specified by the time this test is written; until then the test uses the gate `orchestra-callers` left in place.
